subject: BlueHarbor RFP: regional hosting exceptions, routing & availability annex
messages:
From: Alice Martin <alice.martin@blueharbor.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: security@blueharbor.com, procurement@blueharbor.com
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: RFP — data residency & regional availability questions (Blue Harbor)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking our RFP. Attached is the spreadsheet of questions the procurement and security teams asked for the hosting/residency sections. The three areas we need clarified urgently:

1) EU-only production hosting — can Redwood guarantee no cross-border model execution for EU-located production workloads?
2) APAC edge availability — we have regional latency SLAs for APAC operations; can you describe how Redwood serves APAC traffic and what exceptions exist (e.g., burst to other regions)?
3) Temporary exceptions — do you allow US-based cache or telemetry exports for operational needs? If so, what controls/audits are available?

We are on a tight timeline and need your formal annex/answers by EOD next Wednesday.

Attached: BlueHarbor-RFP-questions.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Regards,
Alice Martin
Procurement, Blue Harbor Logistics
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Alice Martin <alice.martin@blueharbor.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFP — data residency & regional availability questions (Blue Harbor)

Alice —

Thanks — we received the spreadsheet and started drafting the annex. High level answers below; we'll follow up with a consolidated PDF and an ops excerpt.

- EU production residency: Redwood Private and Redwood Dedicated both support EU-primary hosting with model execution and data processing pinned to EU zones. For hosted customers we provide an EU-only tenancy option; this ensures inference execution, KV/prefix caches, and persisted logs remain in EU regions.

- APAC edge availability: We operate a multi-region routing policy. For low-latency APAC reads we prefer APAC edges when available; in constrained capacity we offer burst-to-compatible variants (quantized models in regional buckets) with explicit opt-in. We can include an availability carve-out for peak-period bursts in the exceptions annex.

- Temporary US cache/telemetry: We generally avoid cross-border egress for customer data. Operational telemetry (aggregated metrics, anonymized traces) may leave a region for platform reliability, but raw request payloads and model contexts remain in-region unless you explicitly authorize a cross-border workflow. All telemetry is encrypted in transit and at rest; keys are customer-managed in Private deployments.

I'll attach: regional-hosting-annex.pdf (draft), data-flow-diagram.svg (high-level). Can your security team confirm specific retention windows for any logs that might be considered operationally necessary to export?

Next steps: I'll circulate a single PDF with explicit statements we can sign off on. If you want legal/ops on a call, propose times and I'll loop in Ben and Neha.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: security@blueharbor.com

Subject: Re: RFP — short clarifications on KV cache and key management

Hi Kimberly,

A couple quick clarifications after reviewing your draft annex:

- KV / prefix cache behavior — if a model is hosted in EU but a cached prefix exists in a US edge, will the inference read the US cache or fetch upstream? We need to ensure no customer PII is served from outside EU boundaries for EU workloads.

- Key management — for Private deployments what KMS integrations do you support for HSM-backed keys? We need to list specific vendors and versions for our procurement checklist.

If possible, please be explicit in the annex: where data may transiently touch a non-EU host and what controls (sampling, redaction, audit) are in place.

Thanks,
Blue Harbor Security
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 09:16:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: RFP — short clarifications on KV cache and key management

Kim — forwarding Blue Harbor's security follow-ups; suggested technical language below (feel free to reuse):

> On Wed, 13 Jan 2027 at 08:34, security@blueharbor.com wrote:
> > if a model is hosted in EU but a cached prefix exists in a US edge, will the inference read the US cache or fetch upstream?

Proposed answer (technical):
- For EU-primary workloads we enforce region-local KV namespace resolution. Edge caches are regionalized by namespace: EU namespaces resolve to EU cache endpoints. If an APAC/US edge receives an EU request it forwards the request to the EU serving pool rather than reading a foreign cache.
- Transient exceptions: under explicit ops-approved emergency play (e.g., failover during region outage) we may route to compatible regional variants; those flows are logged, sampled (1%), and require a pre-approved exception ticket. No PII is served from foreign caches without explicit authorization.

KMS note: For Private deployments we support AWS KMS (incl. multi-Region keys), Azure Key Vault, and customer-hosted PKCS#11-compatible HSMs (YubiHSM/Thales via PKCS#11). We'll include version ranges in the annex.

I've attached an excerpt from the ops playbook you can include (ops_playbook_excerpt.txt) that describes emergency failover tickets and logging.

Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Subject: Blue Harbor RFP — formal annex and operational commitments (attached)

Alice / Blue Harbor team —

Attached please find our formal annex and responses to your residency and availability questions: BlueHarbor-RFP-answers-20270118.pdf. Summary of commitments and clarifications below (for your legal/procurement checklist):

1) EU Production Residency Guarantee
- Redwood will pin inference execution and customer model contexts to EU region(s) for any tenant that selects the "EU-primary" tenancy during provisioning. This includes serving runtime, persisted KV namespaces, and persisted logs. No inference execution will occur outside EU regions for EU-primary production by default.

2) Edge routing & APAC availability
- We operate regional edges in APAC and maintain model variants (full-precision and quantized) per region. APAC traffic is routed to APAC edges; if APAC capacity is exhausted the system can perform controlled bursts to compatible regional variants. Bursts require pre-authorized exception (we can include a contractual carve-out with defined thresholds).

3) Transient cross-border telemetry / cache exceptions
- Operational telemetry (aggregated metrics, anonymized traces) may leave region for platform health. Raw request payloads and KV contents remain in-region unless you authorize cross-border processing. Emergency failovers are treated as exceptions: they are ticketed, logged, and audited. We will not serve customer-identifiable PII from a foreign cache without explicit authorization.

4) Key management and encryption
- Private: AWS KMS (including multi-region keys), Azure Key Vault, and PKCS#11-compatible HSMs supported.
- Hosted: platform-managed encryption by default; customer-supplied KMS available for Dedicated/Private.

Next steps
- We can provide our SOC 2 Type II report and a redlineable annex for signature. Please confirm: (A) retention window acceptable for operational logs that may be exported (suggest 30 days by default), and (B) whether you want the APAC burst carve-out in the contract.

Attachments:
- BlueHarbor-RFP-answers-20270118.pdf (formal annex)
- regional-hosting-annex.pdf (technical appendix)
- data-flow-diagram.svg (illustration)

If useful, I'll set up a 30-min technical review with Ben and Neha for Friday.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
